title: The India-Nepal Boundary Issue
description: Context: Nepal’s newly elected Prime Minister, Balendra Shah Balen, has fundamentally shifted the diplomatic discourse by calling for a rational, objective approach to resolving the long-standing Kalapani, Lipulekh, and Limpiyadhura boundary disputes with India. Historical Backgound: The Root of the Dispute: The Shifting Political Tone in Kathmandu: The emergence of a new, youth-led administration in Kathmandu offers a unique opportunity to build a modern, enlightened partnership between India and Nepal. title: Reimagining the India-Nepal Partnership
description: This editorial is based on “New and raw: On Nepal-India ties” published in The Hindu on 10/06/2026. The article explores recent diplomatic outreach between India and Nepal, arguing that stabilizing relations requires both nations to move beyond historical baggage and territorial friction toward a resilient, future-oriented partnership. For Prelims: UPI, G20, Surya Kiran, Earthquake, National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Ramayana Circuit, SAARC, BIMSTEC, BBIN, Kalapani-Limpiyadhura-Lipulekh Trijunction, 1816 Treaty of Sugauli, Kali River, Belt and Road Initiative (BRI), Non-tariff Barriers, Pancheshwar Multipurpose Project, Kailash Mansarovar. For Mains: Areas of convergence and divergence between India and Nepal, Steps needed to strengthen India-Nepal bilateral relations. Nepal’s new leadership is visiting New Delhi to stabilize bilateral relations, seeking to overcome historical tensions and "cycles of mistrust" regarding territorial disputes and engagement with third-party nations like China and the United Kingdom on border issues. Both nations are prioritizing constructive cooperation on critical issues like energy, trade, infrastructure, and border management to move past previous friction and build a stronger partnership.
